summary: Phase 0 complete. Claude Code and Codex CLI pass all checks with the correct flags. Antigravity CLI (agy) has one confirmed, unresolved gap: --mode plan does not block writes.

report.name: claude
report.notes: Deny-by-default headless mode is --permission-mode dontAsk. bypassPermissions + --disallowedTools does NOT enforce the deny list (confirmed: file was written anyway, permission_denials was empty). Default/plan permission modes hang indefinitely with no TTY to approve — always pair -p with an explicit permission mode.

report.name: codex
report.notes: codex exec reads additional prompt content from stdin and hangs forever if stdin is a piped, unclosed stream — must call child.stdin.end() (or redirect from /dev/null) on every invocation. --json emits JSONL; final answer is the last {"type":"item.completed","item":{"type":"agent_message","text":...}} event. --sandbox read-only correctly blocks writes; workspace-write correctly allows them.

report.name: agy
report.nativeTimeout: respected directionally but ~2x overhead (3s requested -> ~6s actual); don't rely on it alone
report.notes: UNRESOLVED GAP: --mode plan does NOT block writes — confirmed twice via direct manual invocation, file was created both times. No alternative flag found yet in --help. Also: without --add-dir <cwd>, agy ignores the working directory entirely and writes into its own scratch dir (~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/scratch) instead. Do not use agy in a reviewer role until this is resolved or OS-level sandboxing (container / read-only bind mount) is added as a backstop.
